name: פְּדָהצוּר
summary: Borne by a man of Manasseh, known only as the father of Gamaliel, the tribe’s leader in the wilderness (Num 1:10; 2:20; 7:54, 59; 10:23). The name is a sentence: the verb פָּדָה, “he has redeemed”, with צוּר, “Rock”, a title scripture gives to Yahweh (Deu 32:4, 15). It names God as the one who sets free, as he had just redeemed Israel from the house of slaves (Deu 7:8).

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Manasseh, Gamaliel בֶּן־פְּדָהצוּר.
For Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, among the men who stood with Moses at the numbering.
The name’s verb with God as its subject: Yahweh “redeemed you (וַיִּפְדְּךָ) from the house of slaves”.
“The Rock (הַצּוּר), his work is perfect”: צוּר as a title of God.
Israel “scorned the Rock of his salvation”.
פְּדַהְאֵל, “God has redeemed”, the same form of name with אֵל.

note: BDB key q.aj.ah. The text writes the name as one word in Num 1:10 and 2:20 and as פְּדָה־צוּר, two words, in Num 7:54, 59 and 10:23, so the database files under this key every צוּר (rock, Zur, Beth-zur) by spelling; the name’s own tokens are only those five verses. Punic names of the type pd-DN, “DN redeem!”, are the same kind of name.
